image_description: A close-up view of a large marine animal, likely a whale, surfacing next to a blue boat hull. The animal's head and upper back are visible above the waterline. The skin is dark grey/black with lighter mottling. There is significant digital distortion or artifacting on the right side where the animal meets the boat/water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible but the angle and resolution obscure the top of the rostrum; blowholes are not clearly distinguishable as two distinct features.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin shows characteristic mottling and lighter patches consistent with barnacle/cyamid infestation found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The posterior back and dorsal area are either submerged or obscured by the boat/artifacting, making this feature impossible to verify.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior portion of the animal is visible; the full body shape cannot be assessed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; visible skin texture matches the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are submerged and not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely out of frame/submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible surface of the head exhibits the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of image, interface between whale and boat
artifact_observations.reasoning: Severe geometric failure where the whale's body seems to merge or clip through the blue boat hull. The edges are nonsensical and lack physical definition.
Indistinct, garbled black shapes resembling text or a watermark that do not form legible characters, typical of AI generation artifacts.
The water interaction lacks realistic displacement and splash dynamics; the water appears somewhat plastic and smudged near the contact points.

alignment_reasoning: The subject is correctly identified as a grey whale based on visible head morphology and skin mottling/callosities. However, most diagnostic checkpoints (dorsal knuckles, body shape, flippers, tail) are untestable due to framing. Among testable features, the skin texture aligns well, but the overall composition is heavily compromised by artifacts.
artifact_reasoning: The image suffers from catastrophic structural artifacts, specifically the fusion/clipping of the whale into the boat hull (severity 4.5). Additionally, there is gibberish text artifacting in the corner and unnatural water textures. These issues significantly degrade the image quality despite the correct biological classification of the visible parts.
